summary: The enterprise AI model API landscape in 2025-2026 is dominated by the three hyperscalers—AWS Bedrock, Azure AI Foundry (formerly Azure OpenAI Service), and Google Vertex AI—which offer governed, VPC-isolated access to foundation models without data leaving the customer's cloud boundary. A second tier led by data-platform players like Snowflake Cortex AI and Databricks has emerged by bringing models directly to governed enterprise data, while IBM watsonx, Oracle Cloud AI, and Cloudflare Workers AI serve specialized compliance, Oracle-native, and edge inference niches. The competitive differentiator has shifted from exclusive model partnerships toward model breadth, data governance, and integration with existing cloud and data contracts.
why_enterprises_use_aggregators: Data residency and privacy: inference runs inside the enterprise's own cloud/VPC so proprietary prompts and data never leave the governed environment or train vendor models
Compliance and governance: built-in audit logs, access controls, SOC 2/HIPAA/FedRAMP/GDPR certifications, and regional isolation satisfy regulatory requirements vendor APIs often can't
Single billing and existing contracts: consumption rolls into existing cloud commitments (EDPs, Azure/AWS/GCP spend) rather than new vendor relationships and procurement cycles
Model diversity with vendor neutrality: one managed API provides access to GPT, Claude, Llama, Gemini, Mistral, and more, avoiding lock-in to any single model provider

Enterprise integration and security: native tie-ins to IAM, KMS encryption, private networking, RAG over governed data, and monitoring reduce engineering overhead versus stitching together raw vendor APIs

platforms.name: AWS Bedrock
platforms.pricing: Pay-per-token (on-demand) with Provisioned Throughput options and Batch discounts; no data used for model training
platforms.best_for: Enterprises wanting the widest model choice and multi-provider access within AWS-native workloads

platforms.name: Azure AI Foundry (Azure OpenAI Service)
platforms.pricing: Pay-per-token with Provisioned Throughput Units (PTUs) for reserved capacity; included in enterprise Azure agreements
platforms.best_for: Enterprises deep in the Microsoft ecosystem needing premier OpenAI models and M365/copilot integration

platforms.name: Google Vertex AI Model Garden
platforms.pricing: Pay-per-token / per-request with Provisioned Throughput and committed-use discounts
key_features: Grounding with Google Search & enterprise data
platforms.best_for: Data-centric and multimodal AI workloads with strong ML pipeline/MLOps needs on GCP

platforms.name: Snowflake Cortex AI
platforms.pricing: Consumption-based using Snowflake credits; billed against existing Snowflake spend
key_features: Models run directly on governed data in Snowflake
platforms.best_for: Organizations running governed, production AI directly on their Snowflake data warehouse

platforms.name: Databricks Mosaic AI
platforms.pricing: Consumption-based (DBUs) with pay-per-token Foundation Model APIs and provisioned throughput
platforms.best_for: Data engineering and ML teams building custom, governed GenAI on the lakehouse

platforms.name: IBM watsonx.ai
platforms.pricing: Resource Unit (RU) token-based pricing; available SaaS or on-prem/hybrid (watsonx on Cloud Pak)
platforms.best_for: Regulated industries needing hybrid/on-prem deployment with strong AI governance and IP indemnification

platforms.name: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI) Generative AI
platforms.pricing: Pay-per-character/token on-demand with dedicated AI clusters for reserved capacity
platforms.best_for: Oracle-centric enterprises and sovereign-cloud deployments integrating GenAI with Oracle apps/databases

platforms.name: Cloudflare Workers AI
platforms.pricing: Pay-per-use billed in 'Neurons' (compute units); low-cost serverless, free tier available
platforms.best_for: Low-latency, globally distributed edge AI and cost-sensitive serverless inference on open models
